t.E1521.agn: In 1979 JECFA set the ADI for PEG at 0–10 mg/kg body weight/day; the SCF had given a group ADI of 5 mg/kg for PEG 300–4000. In 2006 EFSA had stated that use in food supplement tablet coatings did not raise a safety concern. In the 2018 exposure assessment, the highest estimated intake (6.1 mg/kg a day, only in supplement users) remained within this ADI range, and it was stated that the estimates very probably overestimated actual intake.
t.E1521.body: Absorption of polyethylene glycols from the gut depends on molecular size: large ones (molecular weight 4000–6000) are almost not absorbed, while small ones are partly absorbed (40–50% of the dose was found in the urine of people taking PEG 400); the absorbed part is excreted in urine.
t.E1521.found.0: Table-top sweeteners in powder and tablet form
t.E1521.found.1: Food supplement capsules and tablets (up to 10,000 mg/kg)
t.E1521.prod: A polymer produced by chemical synthesis, through addition polymerisation of ethylene oxide with water.
t.E1521.regx.0: Exposure re-evaluated; the highest estimate within the SCF and JECFA ADI range.
t.E1521.summary: A synthetic polymer. Used as a coating and carrier in supplement tablets.
t.E1521.what: It is polyethylene glycol (PEG); used in tablet coatings and as a carrier in sweeteners.
